transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

Lately I can’t seem to focus on my analyses at work—my mind keeps going blank even when I’m staring right at the spreadsheets. It's gotten to the point where it's really affecting my day-to-day tasks, and I wanted to get some help figuring out what's going on.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood, such as feeling sad, empty, or hopeless, alongside these difficulties with focus and concentration?
No, I wouldn't say I feel sad, empty, or hopeless. It's more that I feel extremely anxious, tense, and constantly wired about work. I just feel completely overwhelmed all the time.

Have you experienced any episodes of intense fear or discomfort that reach a peak within minutes, accompanied by symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or trembling, which might be contributing to your feelings of being overwhelmed?

No, I haven't experienced any sudden, intense episodes like that or things like a racing heart. My anxiety feels more like a constant, non-stop mental worry and tension that hangs over me all day. It's just a continuous stream of worrying rather than sudden physical panic attacks.
Have you found yourself avoiding certain tasks, situations, or places because of your anxiety or worries, or are you still able to engage with your daily activities despite feeling overwhelmed?

Yes, I’ve started avoiding social activities, like skipping runs with my running club and turning down plans with friends because I feel too wired and behind on work to enjoy them. I still force myself to do my job, but my performance has suffered and I've even missed a couple of minor deadlines lately. It's just really hard to fully engage in anything else right now.

Can you tell me more about how your anxiety and avoidance of social activities are affecting your relationships with family and friends, and if you've noticed any significant changes in your overall daily routine?

My relationships have definitely suffered because I keep turning down friends and skipped my running club, feeling too wired and behind to actually show up and enjoy myself. My entire daily routine has been taken over by work, with me working late into the night and obsessively checking emails on weekends. Even my sleep is completely ruined now because I lie awake until 2 or 3 a.m. replaying work scenarios in my head.

Do you find that your excessive worry and anxiety are specifically focused on a particular aspect of your life, such as work, or do they seem to be more generalized and encompass many different areas of your life?

It definitely started with work, but now the worry has spread to almost every part of my life. I can't even watch a show or enjoy a trip without my mind snowballing into worst-case scenarios, and I even obsess over minor daily things like whether I remembered to lock my apartment door. It just feels like I can't turn the anxiety off, no matter what I'm doing.
Can you describe how often and for how long you find yourself caught up in these cycles of negative thinking and worry, and if there are any specific thoughts or themes that keep repeating?

This worry is almost constant and has been my daily reality for about 15 months now, ever since I started my new role. Even if I try to distract myself, "what-if" thoughts sneak back in within minutes and snowball into fears of making a tiny typo that ruins a client relationship or getting put on a performance plan. It also includes minor daily worries, like obsessing over whether I locked my apartment door, and I can't remember the last time I felt genuinely relaxed.
Have you experienced any physical symptoms like headaches, muscle tension, or gastrointestinal problems that seem to coincide with your periods of heightened anxiety and worry?
I haven't really experienced headaches or stomach issues, luckily. But I do carry a lot of constant physical tension in my body, and I just feel completely exhausted all the time.
You mentioned feeling completely wired and exhausted all the time, can you tell me more about what you mean by 'wired' and if you've experienced any restlessness or an inability to relax physically?

By "wired," I mean that my mind and body constantly feel like they are on high alert and running on adrenaline, even when I'm physically exhausted. I can't remember the last time I felt genuinely relaxed, because whenever I try to sit down and watch a show or read, my mind immediately gets hijacked by those "what-if" scenarios.

You mentioned that your worry initially started with work but has now spread to almost every part of your life. Can you clarify if there are any aspects of your life that remain unaffected by these worries, or has the anxiety become pervasive across all areas?

It has become completely pervasive, and I honestly can't think of any area of my life that is unaffected anymore. It completely ruins simple attempts to relax, like reading or watching a show, and it has totally disrupted my social life with my friends and running club. It even bleeds into mundane daily things, like constantly obsessing over whether I locked my apartment door.
